metadata.title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Support lm_head LoRA for Qwen3.5 with DFlash2 speculative decoding
metadata.body:
## Summary

Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.8 models cannot serve a LoRA adapter that targets `lm_head`. The fix has three small parts:

1. **`qwen3_5.py`**: add `embedding_modules = {"lm_head": "output_embeddings"}` to `Qwen3_5ForCausalLMBase`. This is the lm_head part of upstream vllm-project/vllm#48850. Without it, the adapter is rejected:
   ```
   While loading .../adapter_vllm, expected target modules in [...] but received ['lm_head']
   ```
2. **`lora/layers/logits_processor.py`**: in this fork, `LogitsProcessor.forward` calls `self._apply_logits_transforms(...)`, which is fork-specific. `LogitsProcessorWithLoRA` reuses that `forward` but does not define the method. Once (1) wraps the logits processor, every request would hit an `AttributeError`. The new method delegates to `base_layer`, the same way the wrapper already handles `scale` and `soft_cap`.
3. **`v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`** + **`LogitsProcessorWithLoRA`**: skip the DFlash2 sparse target path (`speculator.try_sample_target`) only for batches that contain an active LoRA request.
   - That path calls `get_topk_tokens_and_logits_with_fallback` / `get_compact_target_probe_with_fallback`, which project with the base `lm_head` directly and would ignore an lm_head LoRA delta. `LogitsProcessorWithLoRA` did not implement them, so before this change any multi-token request with draft tokens failed once LoRA was enabled:
     ```
     AttributeError: 'LogitsProcessorWithLoRA' object has no attribute 'get_topk_tokens_and_logits_with_fallback'
     ```
   - The runner now checks `self.lora_state.lora_ids[input_batch.idx_mapping_np].any()`. Batches with a LoRA request use the existing dense, LoRA-aware rejection sampling. Batches without one keep the sparse path, so base-model traffic on a `--enable-lora` server is not slowed down.
   - The wrapper delegates the sparse methods to `base_layer`, which is correct because they are only reached for LoRA-free batches. `allow_graph=self.lora_config is None` is unchanged.

4. **`v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`**: map lm_head LoRA per logits row, not per request, under speculative decoding.
   - `LoraState.make_lora_inputs` returns one `prompt_lora_mapping` entry per request, but with draft tokens each request has `1 + num_draft` logits rows (`cu_num_logits`). The punica logits kernel only covers the first `num_reqs` rows and in request order, so lm_head LoRA deltas land on the wrong rows or are missing.
   - Symptom: an adapter request's output distribution shifts whenever another request in the same batch is decoding with drafts. In our test the adapter's top choice probability dropped from 0.633 (alone) to 0.552 (alongside one decoding chat). Prefill-only concurrency did not shift it.
   - Fix: repeat the mapping by `np.diff(input_batch.cu_num_logits_np)` when the batch has draft tokens (the older GPU runner in upstream vLLM does the same with `num_sampled_tokens`).

## Testing

Hardware: 2x V100-32GB, TP=2, `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8`, DFlash2 speculative decoding, `--enable-lora --max-lora-rank 32`.

The engine ran the v1.5.1 release wheel with the same three changes applied. On v1.5.1 the runner hunk wraps `try_dflash2_sparse_target_rejection(...)` directly. On `main` it wraps `speculator.try_sample_target(...)`, which has the same meaning.

Adapter: [`autotrust/JEV-27B`](https://huggingface.co/autotrust/JEV-27B) `adapter_vllm` (r=32, targets the GDN/attention/MLP projections plus `lm_head`).

- Engine starts with the adapter registered. No errors.
- Adapter outputs (`/v1/completions`, `max_tokens=1`, `allowed_token_ids`, `processed_logprobs`) match the probabilities in the adapter's model card. Example choice case: `[0.233, 0.132, 0.634, 0.001]` here vs `[0.254, 0.125, 0.620, 0.001]` on the card (bf16 vs FP8 base). The base model without the adapter gives `[0.101, 0.066, 0.763, 0.070]`.
- Ablation copies of the adapter (lm_head-only vs. lm_head `lora_B` zeroed) show the lm_head delta changes the output distribution, so the wrapped logits processor is in use and not bypassed.
- Base-model chat (no adapter) with DFlash2 runs 300-token generations at 65-108 tok/s (single request), back on the sparse path. Spec-decode metrics show drafts being accepted.
- Requests that use the adapter generate long outputs correctly on the dense path (slower, as expected).
- Mixed concurrent load (3 base chats + 1 adapter chat + adapter decisions) completes with no errors in the engine log.
- With fix 4, adapter decisions alongside 1-2 decoding chats (base or adapter) stay at 0.617-0.623 vs 0.633 alone (the residual matches prefill-only concurrency, i.e. normal batching numerics); before the fix they were 0.550-0.553. All five model-card example cases stay within ~0.03 of the card under load.
- Base-model temp-0 chat output is identical whether the concurrent load is base-model or adapter requests.

Not run: the repository unit test suites (no CI-equivalent environment here).

## Notes (not changed in this PR)

- **Adapter key prefix.** Adapters trained on the text-only model (keys `base_model.model.model.layers.*`) load into `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` without errors, but `hf_to_vllm_mapper` only maps `model.language_model.` and `lm_head.`. Every body LoRA module is therefore silently unmatched, and only `lm_head` takes effect. Renaming the keys to `base_model.model.model.language_model.layers.*` fixed it in our test. A mapper entry for `model.layers.` might be the proper fix, but it also affects base checkpoint loading, so it is left to maintainers.
- **Gate granularity.** The gate checks for any active LoRA, not specifically an lm_head LoRA. Adapters without lm_head could in principle keep the sparse path; kept simple here.
